name: Iri
overview: Iri was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the son of Bela. His identity is primarily established through this unique attribute, with no additional notes provided. This places him within the genealogical records of Israel as found in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Iri appears as a proper name in Scripture and is possibly derived from a term meaning 'donkey’s colt,' indicating a likely Hebrew origin. A closely related name, Ir, meaning 'stallion donkey,' is also found in the same tribal context, though it is not explicitly stated to refer to the same individual. Neither name is recorded as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Iri as the son of Bela. Additionally, it can be inferred that he was the father of Muppim and Huppim, although these relationships are not stated outright. Beyond these, no further family details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Iri's significance lies in his place within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Benjamin, serving as a link in the lineage that preserves the heritage and identity of God's chosen people. As the son of Bela, he represents a continuation of the tribe's descendants, which is important for understanding the broader biblical narrative of Israel's history and God's covenant promises. Though not a prominent figure in terms of narrative action, his inclusion in the genealogies underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His people through generations.
